heard: 1,100-mile cloud appears over a Martian volcano every morning. It races westward at 380 miles per hour, then vanishes before noon. The cloud grows high above Arceomons, a volcano 12 miles tall. ESA tracked this daily lifecycle using an ordinary webcam on Mars Express. Earth clouds need dust or pollen particles to freeze around, but Arceomons forces air upward, dropping temperatures 54 degrees in 10 minutes. Water vapor freezes spontaneously straight out of clean air. spontaneous freezing creates a massive spectacle every sunrise.
